questions.q: Why do teams usually aim by tilting the hood instead of by changing the flywheel speed?
questions.correct: The light hood re-aims instantly, but the heavy flywheel is slow to change speed
wrong: The flywheel is locked by the rules and its speed can never be changed
The hood is the only part on the whole robot that is allowed to move
Changing the flywheel speed would launch the ball in the totally wrong direction
questions.explain: The flywheel is heavy, so changing its RPM takes time — that's why it sags after a shot. The hood is light, so a new angle is there instantly. Teams hold one steady flywheel speed and do their aiming with the quick hood.

questions.q: What kind of servo is the hood?
questions.correct: A positional servo that drives to an exact angle and holds it
wrong: A continuous-rotation servo that only spins and never holds a set angle
A DC motor with an encoder that counts its own turning ticks
A stepper motor that clicks forward just one tooth at a time
questions.explain: The hood needs a precise, held angle, so it is a positional Servo (a 'Pointer'): setPosition(angle) drives it to that exact spot and holds it. A CRServo only sets a speed and can't hold a known angle.

questions.q: In code, which call moves a positional servo like the hood?
wrong: hood.setPower(0.6)
hood.spinTo(0.6)
hood.setVelocity(0.6)
questions.explain: A positional Servo uses setPosition(value), where value is 0.0 to 1.0 — an angle it drives to and holds. setPower and setVelocity command a speed, which is for CR servos and motors.

questions.q: In a rack-and-pinion hood, what does the servo turn directly?
questions.correct: A small round gear called the pinion
wrong: The curved rack built onto the hood
The hood hinge pin, spun by hand
The spinning flywheel mounted behind it
questions.explain: The servo turns a small round gear (the pinion). Its teeth mesh with the curved row of teeth (the rack) on the hood, so turning the pinion walks along the rack and tilts the hood.

questions.q: Where are the rack teeth in the hood mechanism?
questions.correct: On the hood itself, as a curved row of teeth
wrong: On the servo's output shaft, right beside the pinion
Around the outer rim of the spinning flywheel wheel
On the drivetrain wheels down at the robot's corners
questions.explain: The rack is the curved set of teeth attached to the hood. The small pinion on the servo meshes into those teeth; as the pinion turns, the hood tilts up or down.

questions.q: Why gear the hood down (a small pinion moving a bigger rack)?
questions.correct: So a small servo turn becomes a precise, steady hood angle
wrong: So the hood snaps to a brand-new angle as fast as possible
So the servo draws far less electric current from the battery
So the flywheel spinning behind it can reach a higher speed
questions.explain: Gearing down means one servo turn makes only a little hood tilt — giving fine, precise control and holding firm against the ball hammering past. It trades speed for precision and holding strength.

questions.q: A very FLAT hood angle sends the ball...
questions.correct: Low and far, so it can overshoot the hive
wrong: High and short, like a steep lobbing arc
Straight up into the air above the robot
Backward, away from the hive toward the robot
questions.explain: A flat hood launches a low, fast line drive that travels far — too flat and it sails past the hive or slams the front wall instead of arcing in.

questions.q: A very HIGH hood angle sends the ball...
questions.correct: High and short, dropping in front of the target
wrong: Low and far, sailing well past the hive
In a perfectly flat line toward the target
Nowhere at all, staying stuck inside the robot
questions.explain: A high hood throws a tall, steep lob. It goes way up but doesn't carry far, so it drops short of the hive. The sweet spot is in the middle.

questions.q: With the flywheel held at one steady speed, the hood angle mainly controls...
questions.correct: Where the shot lands — its aim and reach
wrong: How fast the heavy flywheel wheel actually spins
The color of the game piece being launched
The driving speed of the whole robot base
questions.explain: Speed comes from the flywheel; the hood sets the launch angle, which changes where the ball lands. Steady speed plus an adjustable angle lets you score from different spots.

questions.q: In the OpMode, which stick axis aims the hood?
wrong: The right stick's up-and-down (Y) axis
The left stick's up-and-down forward axis
The dpad's up-and-down direction buttons
questions.explain: Right stick left/right calls robot.hood.aim(gamepad1.right_stick_x). Up/down on that stick trims the flywheel target. One stick: up/down = how hard, left/right = how high.

questions.q: What does aim(amount) do each loop?
questions.correct: Nudges the stored position a little, then clamps it
wrong: Jumps the hood straight to one fixed preset angle
Spins the hood around and around without ever stopping
Turns the flywheel on and fires off a shot
questions.explain: aim() ignores tiny stick drift (a deadzone), then creeps position up or down by a small step and clamps it between HOOD_MIN and HOOD_MAX — the same trim-a-little-each-loop pattern the flywheel target uses.

questions.q: Why does aim() clamp position between HOOD_MIN and HOOD_MAX?
questions.correct: To keep the hood inside its safe travel range
wrong: To make the hood swing between angles much faster
To save battery power while the robot is driving
To reverse the servo's turning direction every single loop
questions.explain: Clamping with Math.max/Math.min keeps position within the servo's real range, so holding the stick can't drive the hood past its limits or command a value below 0.0 or above 1.0.

questions.correct: Reporting the current hood setting on the telemetry
wrong: Moving the hood over to a brand-new angle
Turning off the flywheel motor between quick shots
Resetting the motor's encoder count back to zero
questions.explain: getPosition() just returns the stored position (0..1) so the OpMode can show it on the Driver Hub. It reads the state — it never changes anything.

questions.q: In update(), what does the hood subsystem do every loop?
questions.correct: Calls hood.setPosition(position) to apply the stored angle
wrong: Calls hood.setPower(position) to spin the hood servo
Does nothing, since the servo just moves itself
Calls flywheel.toggle() to fire off a quick shot
questions.explain: Every loop, update() applies the state: hood.setPosition(position). The positional servo drives to that exact angle and holds it. That is the 'apply the state' step of the subsystem pattern.

questions.q: Why is a positional servo, not a CR servo, the right pick for the hood?
questions.correct: Aiming needs an exact held angle, which it provides
wrong: CR servos simply cost more money than positional ones
The hood must spin around in complete full circles
Positional servos are faster than any big drive motor
questions.explain: Aiming means holding a precise, unchanging angle. A positional Servo goes to an exact position and stays there. A CRServo only sets a speed and can't hold a known angle, so it can't aim.
